claim: Archive POKs cannot be imported blindly: check each against the disassembly, translate addresses, and test every one per release.

evidence.text: One entry of the archive's .pok is an address in the packed snapshot (54462, lives), the rest are live addresses that the unpack overwrites; tested on the real game, translated through the stream map.
evidence.quote: One entry of the archive's .pok is an address in the packed snapshot (54462, lives), the rest are live addresses that the unpack overwrites

evidence.text: The .pok's [L1] lines name addresses of another release (data or mid-instruction in this file); only Infinite Lives (34919) and the unlabelled-version lines 35604 and 35651 work here, proven on the simulator.
evidence.quote: only Infinite Lives (34919) and the unlabelled-version lines 35604 and 35651 work here, proven on the simulator

evidence.text: The TOSEC .pok's Infinite Lives also pokes 34925, which is not lives but a graphics pointer (read by the plotter's frame lookup at 39837); the single-poke trainer is used.
evidence.quote: the TOSEC .pok's Infinite Lives also pokes 34925, which is not lives but a graphics pointer

evidence.text: Of 16 .pok trainers, See Ending and Paralyzed Enemies freeze the game, Keep SabreMan cyan sets colour 186 and stops the orchid effects ending, Immunity still loses lives; the menu keeps the six shown to work.
